summary: Order quote timeouts originate in pricing-engine, not the reported order-service or market-data-service. A config/feature-flag change cfg-3120 at 12:04Z ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5% to 100%, routing all quote traffic through the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (2.9-8.9s per quote). pricing-engine CPU jumped from ~40% to ~99% (with request rate flat), quote deadlines (2000ms budget) were exceeded, p99 rose to ~2.6s and 5xx to ~12.5%, and order-service quote calls timed out at 2500ms starting 12:06:10Z. The market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy (dep-6111, 11:56Z) is a temporal red herring: its latency/CPU stayed flat and the onset follows the flag ramp, not the deploy. Root cause category: config_change.

ranked_hypotheses.title: greeks_v2 flag ramp to 100% saturated pricing-engine CPU, causing quote deadline misses
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 at 12:04Z ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5% to 100%, so the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (2.9-8.9s per quote) ran for all traffic, pinning pricing-engine CPU at ~99%. Quotes exceeded the 2000ms budget and pricing-engine returned latency/errors, so order-service quote calls hit their 2500ms timeout. Fault originates at pricing-engine (config_change).

causal_chain.claim: GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo runs for all traffic, taking multi-second per quote
pricing-engine CPU saturates ~99% with flat request rate
order-service quote calls time out at 2500ms

assumptions: The 5%->100% ramp is what newly routed the expensive GreeksV2 path; the calculator itself was already deployed but only sampled.

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf serialization deploy degraded quote path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deployment dep-6111 (market-data-service v5.2.0, protobuf quote serialization) at 11:56Z caused pricing-engine quote slowdowns leading to order-service timeouts.
assumptions: Serialization overhead could be CPU-bound in pricing-engine even without market-data-service degradation.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service latency (~40ms) and CPU (~45%) are flat across the window (F7); onset is 12:05-12:06 (F3), ~10 min after the 11:56 deploy and ~immediately after the 12:04 flag ramp (F2). The deploy is a temporal red herring.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity saturation from market-open load
ranked_hypotheses.statement: pricing-engine was overwhelmed by organic request-volume growth (as in HIST-113), exhausting provisioned capacity.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate is flat ~635-661 req/s before and after onset (F5/tc-013); the CPU rise coincides with the flag ramp, not with a traffic increase.

facts.statement: order-service quote timeouts started 12:06:10Z (225 errors of 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms').
Config change cfg-3120 ramped greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100 at 12:04:00Z.
GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo computations took 2.9-8.9s and quote deadlines (2000ms budget) began being exceeded at 12:05:21Z.
pricing-engine p99 latency rose from ~60ms to ~2600-2800ms and error_rate to ~12.5%, while request_rate stayed flat ~640 req/s.
market-data-service latency and CPU stayed flat across the incident window.
The only deployment was market-data-service dep-6111 at 11:56Z (protobuf serialization), preceding symptoms by ~10 minutes.
pricing-engine memory stayed ~49% and restarts stayed 0, indicating no node/memory failure.

assumptions: The greeks_v2 flag controls whether quotes use the GreeksV2 calculator; at 5% only a fraction of traffic paid the cost, so CPU stayed ~40%.
The 2000ms pricing-engine deadline and 2500ms order-service timeout are as logged.

timeline.event: cfg-3120 ramps greeks_v2 rollout_pct 5->100 on pricing-engine
First GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo slow log (6465ms) on pricing-engine

recommended_actions.action: Roll back cfg-3120 (set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back toward 5%) to restore pricing-engine CPU and quote latency.
recommended_actions.rationale: Onset coincides exactly with the 5%->100% ramp; reverting should remove the CPU saturation.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback is not possible, shed/limit GreeksV2 traffic or scale pricing-engine replicas temporarily.
recommended_actions.rationale: CPU is pinned at ~99%; adding capacity or reducing load restores headroom.

recommended_actions.action: Optimize or bound the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (reduce paths or cache) before re-ramping.
recommended_actions.rationale: 20000-path Monte-Carlo takes multi-second per quote, far above the 2000ms budget.

recommended_actions.action: Add a canary/gradual-ramp guard with CPU and p99 SLO gates for pricing feature-flag rollouts.
recommended_actions.rationale: A 5%->100% single-step ramp on a CPU-heavy path bypassed any staged validation.

data_gaps: config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond on first query (tc-004 partial); a second query returned the single cfg-3120 change, but a config change in the missing shard cannot be fully excluded.
No pre-12:04 log lines explicitly stating the greeks_v2 effective rollout percentage beyond the single applied-change line (tc-016).

findings.statement: pricing-engine latency_p99_ms jumped from ~60ms (11:30-11:50) to 1325ms avg in the 12:00 bucket and ~2600-2700ms sustained thereafter, max 2849ms.
pricing-engine cpu_pct rose from ~40% (11:30-11:50) to avg 99.27% at 12:10 and stayed ~99% through 13:59 (max 100%), while request_rate remained flat ~635-661 req/s.
pricing-engine error_rate (HTTP 5xx) rose from ~0.2% to 12.55% avg at 12:10 and stayed ~12.4-12.7% through 13:59.
market-data-service latency_p99_ms stayed flat ~40ms and cpu_pct flat ~45% across 11:30-13:59 (no degradation).
The only deployment in window is dep-6111 (market-data-service v5.2.0, 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf') deployed at 11:56:00Z, not rolled back.
pricing-engine memory_pct stayed flat ~49% and restarts stayed at 0 across the whole window.
order-service depends on pricing-engine via HTTP; pricing-engine depends on market-data-service via HTTP.

Inference: the fault propagates order-service -> pricing-engine, where the CPU-bound GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator exceeds the 2000ms quote deadline, so order-service quote calls hit their 2500ms timeout.
